open_obligations: Check that the helpful/sneaky role conditioning is the main change from Anil et al.'s game.
Note Kirchner et al. state LLM training does not meet the unrestricted prover-class assumption.
Check the two ordering conditions on prover reward (Eq. 1).
out.other_title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
out.rationale: Anil et al. prove verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria are necessary and sufficient for complete and sound protocols when the prover always argues for label 1. Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 proves the same equivalence for a game where the follower is a role-conditioned helpful or sneaky prover with their utilities RV and RP, assuming the prover class is all deterministic mappings.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium as the condition for completeness and soundness, with a role-conditioned helpful/sneaky prover

text: The authors prove (Theorem 1) that, assuming the prover class H is the set of all deterministic mappings from problems to solutions, in the prover-verifier game with verifier utility RV and prover utility RP, the existence of a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium (v*, h*, s*) is necessary and sufficient for the completeness and soundness properties to hold.
title: Verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff completeness and soundness
